newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Subdued Irish bonds shrug off US data,ignore gilts.
newsitem.headline: Subdued Irish bonds shrug off US data,ignore gilts.

text.p: Irish government bonds ticked up in thin, directionless trade on Monday afternoon, but largely ignored a brief surge in U.S. Treasuries, spurred by bond-friendly data, dealers said.
U.S. Treasuries rose after personal income and spending data were in line with expectations and a University of Michigan survey was below forecast.

"It would take something quite exceptional to move the Irish market," one bond dealer said, adding that turnover was very light as most operators were not keen to disturb their books so close to the Christmas holiday.
He said the market did not react to a late rise in gilts on the back of the firmer U.S. market.
By 1630 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 had gained three pence to 101.50 to yield 6.12 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 inched up five pence to 108.80 to yield 6.73 percent.
